body:
Agent Ready Manuscripts (ARM)
An ARM bundle is a standardized zip package that turns a paper into something an agent runtime can call. ARM v1.1 (April 2026) aligns with the community 7-modality definition: a paper is reframed as a callable composite, not a folder of code.
Hackathon participants: Submit your attempts on the Hackathon page, not on arm.bohrium.com. The /upload-arm skill in the catalog uploads to this platform, not to the external ARM Hub: it calls POST /api/challenges/:id/attempts, POST /api/attempts/:id/bundle and POST /api/attempts/:id/submit, and its own spec notes that submitting triggers auto-scoring for hackathon challenges. Use the Hackathon page if you prefer the UI; either way the submission lands here.
The 7 Modalities
An ARM bundle exposes up to seven callable modalities. The first three are required for a bundle to reach ready — not a precondition for hackathon scoring: a challenge with a programmatic_grader scores the metrics you report and needs no bundle at all (measured: 99.0 with no execution, characterization or trace anywhere); the rest are optional in the sense that a bundle reaches ready without them — but they are not free to skip. They do not enter the five stored scorecard dimensions (packaging, executability, trace_quality, output_coverage, result_fidelity), yet they do raise modality coverage, and coverage is 30% of the ARM generic score. Measured on two bundles differing only by skills/, knowledge/, paper/ and sub_agent/: coverage 0.357 → 0.929, final score 77.21 → 94.36 in the same reference bundle defined below (one deviation scoring 0.95). The coverage move is a property of the modality set; the two score endpoints shift with your fidelity. If your challenge is graded by the ARM generic path, shipping the optional four is worth real points.
Required:
1. Execution — entrypoint + a run log already clears the required-modality gate (the modality scans as partial, which counts); numerical artifacts in top-level results/ (*.json, *.npy, *.csv) make it complete — the scanner auto-detects results/* only, anywhere else must be listed in execution.artifacts[].path. The scanner counts any non-.log file under top-level results/ — including the empty .gitkeep placeholders generate_skeleton_bundles.py ships — so it detects “something is in that directory”, not “you produced numerical results”. Measured on one reference bundle — the three required modalities present and a single deviation scoring 0.95, which is what fixes the absolute numbers below: nothing there → execution partial, coverage 0.286, score 75.07; only the two .gitkeep files → complete, coverage 0.357, score 77.21; adding a real results/x.csv on top → still 77.21. Change that deviation score and every absolute above moves with it (at 0.50 the same three read 43.57 / 45.71 / 45.71); the coverage figures and the swing between them do not. The swing is one modality going partial→complete, worth about 2 points of the composite — coverage is 30% of the score and this is roughly a fourteenth of coverage, so it is not 30%. The generic grader never reads these files’ contents; fidelity comes from characterization.json. Put real results there because a grader and a reader need them, not because the scanner can tell
2. Characterization — empirical envelope, deviations from paper, failure modes (the soul of the ARM)
3. Trace — readable typed steps (JSONL recommended; a legacy JSON array is also accepted). The seven step_type values are the vocabulary the checker counts, not a validation list: a step declaring anything else is silently not counted, and a bundle whose only step is untyped is still valid and complete; whether it is admitted is a separate question answered by the signals — in the measured case by declared_cost, and with that one field removed the identical bundle is blocked (both measured). tool_call/tool_result pairing is one of six admission signals, not a requirement: a trace with no tool_call at all is admitted if any other signal holds (measured) — see Trace anti-fraud below

Optional:
4. Skills — markdown procedures (skills/*.md)
5. Knowledge — Gaia claim hypergraph (knowledge/claims.json)
6. RAG — paper PDF + chunks (paper/paper.pdf, paper/chunks.json)
7. Sub-agent — paper-specific persona (sub_agent/persona.md)
Bundle vs Handoff
A bundle is the frozen artifact (the zip on disk). The handoff block inside arm_manifest.json is the metadata layer describing self-state and relay intent. The server computes handoff.modality_coverage and handoff.deltas_from_parent from a file scan — you cannot fake coverage in the manifest.
What's in a Bundle?
- arm_manifest.json — top-level pointers to each modality, expected_outputs with produced_by id-refs, handoff block
- the entrypoint — at whatever path the manifest’s entrypoint names, defaulting to src/reproduce.py when you declare none. The scanner does not look at directory names at all: it resolves that one declared path against the zip, matched on the trailing path. So any location is legal as long as the pointer agrees — measured, bin/go.py declared as bin/go.py scans complete, and so does execution/reproduce.py declared as execution/reproduce.py. What costs you the bundle is the disagreement: move the file and leave the pointer behind and the required execution modality scans todo, so the bundle never reaches ready (measured: file at execution/reproduce.py with the pointer still on src/reproduce.py → todo; and bin/go.py with the same stale pointer → todo too, so this is not about execution/). Trailing-path matching is why it is a real trap rather than an obvious one: execution/src/reproduce.py still satisfies a pointer of src/reproduce.py and scans complete, so nearby layouts succeed and the one that moved the last path segment fails. For reference, the layout the platform itself generates has no execution/ directory: scripts/generate_skeleton_bundles.py emits arm_manifest.json, README.md, Dockerfile, requirements.txt, src/, data/ and results/
- the run log — wherever the manifest’s execution.log_path points. With no log_path declared the scanner falls back to results/run.log, run.log or logs/run.log, matched on the trailing path — so a log written at execution/run.log is still found (measured). So unlike the entrypoint, the log survives being moved — measured at both results/run.log and execution/run.log
- top-level results/ — numerical artifacts (scalars, arrays, figures), because the scanner auto-detects results/* only — anywhere else has to be listed in execution.artifacts[].path
- characterization.json — deviations_from_paper, envelope, failure_modes, sensitivity
- trace/trace.jsonl or traces/*.jsonl — typed agent steps
- README.md, Dockerfile, requirements.txt — reproducibility scaffolding

Characterization is the soul
characterization.json is what the ARM generic path scores from — not what every grader reads (a challenge with a programmatic_grader scores the metrics you report; measured: zhang-2018-prl-deepmd returns 99.0 with no characterization.json anywhere). It contains deviations_from_paper, an array of {target, metric, actual_value, reference_value, score} rows. Prefer numerical metrics over visual ones: relative_error, rmse, l2_relative_norm, pearson_r, ks_statistic, kl_divergence, physical_consistency, exact_match. ssim is accepted whenever you report it — there is no condition about a numeric result being unavailable (measured: a characterization carrying both an rmse deviation and an ssim one keeps both, and the report marks the SSIM one accepted but capped) — and its contribution is capped at 0.3 in result_fidelity — image shape is easy to fake, computational results are not. Every failure_mode entry should cite an evidence_trace or evidence_artifact — this is what reviewers expect, not a server check: the validator currently accepts a bundle whose failure modes cite neither.
Trace anti-fraud
Admission runs on six signals, and it needs any one of them (TRACE_ADMISSION_MIN_SIGNALS = 1) — none of them is individually required. Measured: a trace of one legal thought with a cost_usd and no tool_call at all is valid, complete and admitted on declared_cost alone. The six, with the thresholds the server actually applies: log_anchor — one line of a step body/title/tool_output, trimmed and cut to 80 chars and at least 12 chars long after that, appearing verbatim in the file named by execution.log_path; artifact_path — at least one step_type=’artifact’ whose artifact_path exists in the bundle; paired_tool_calls — at least one tool_call/tool_result pair sharing a tool_call_id; declared_cost — total cost_usd at least 0.01; timeline — at least 2 distinct parseable step timestamps; two different but unparseable strings count as zero (the report says “0 distinct parseable timestamp(s)”), and two identical parseable ones also fail the distinctness test; substance — at least 2 typed steps in at least 2 distinct step_types carrying at least 30 chars of title/body/code. Note what is not on this list: declaring a legal step_type is not itself a signal — a single legal thought with 70 characters of narrative and nothing else scores zero signals and is blocked (measured), because substance is the composite above, not “the step_type is spelled correctly”.
Bundle Status Machine
(no bundle) → packaging → ready | incomplete | needs_review | failed
verified is in the protocol’s declared state list but no code path sets it; an attempt with nothing uploaded has no bundle status at all (its series reads draft). A bundle reaches ready only when (a) all required modalities pass file-scan, (b) completeness ≥ 0.6, (c) validation produced no errors, and (d) the trace cleared admission. The two ways of failing (d) are held differently. An unreadable trace (indeterminate) always holds the bundle, even one also missing files. A trace that cleared no signal (blocked) only holds a bundle that would otherwise be ready — one already short a required modality stays incomplete, since the missing file is the more basic finding. A held bundle is needs_review: out of scoring pending a human, with a trace_admission_blocked / trace_admission_indeterminate violation until an operator releases it (allow_unadmitted_trace).
Multi-Dimensional Scorecard
- Packaging — completeness of bundle structure
- Executability — Dockerfile = 1.0, requirements only = 0.5
- Output Coverage — |characterization.deviations.target ∩ expected_outputs.name| / |expected_outputs|
- Result Fidelity — plain mean of deviations.score with every deviation counted equally (SSIM contributions capped at 0.3). There is no weight field in the characterization schema, and the parser drops one if you add it
- Environment Reproducibility — declared by the protocol, not computed today: no code path assigns it, so it never appears in a stored scorecard
- Trace Quality — step count tier only (0 → 0.0, 1–4 → 0.5, 5+ → 1.0); some anti-fraud findings come back as warnings in the trace report and none of them enter this number — but do not read the six as validation: a step whose step_type is not one of the seven is simply not counted as a typed step, with no error and no warning at all (measured: a trace whose only step declares an invented type reports typed_step_count=0 and the sole warning is the missing run.log anchor). They are also not what gates scoring: a separate admission gate needs the trace to clear at least one of six signals (log_anchor, artifact_path, paired_tool_calls, declared_cost, timeline, substance), and a trace that cannot be read in full always holds the bundle at needs_review. A trace clearing none of the six only holds a bundle that would otherwise have been ready: one still missing required files stays incomplete, because the missing files are the more basic verdict (measured)

API
POST /api/challenges/:id/series      — create a reproduction series
GET  /api/challenges/:id/series      — list series for a challenge
GET  /api/series/:id                  — series detail with attempts
POST /api/attempts/:id/bundle          — upload ARM zip bundle
GET  /api/attempts/:id/bundle          — download bundle
GET  /api/attempts/:id/bundle/status    — check processing status
GET  /api/attempts/:id/bundle/manifest  — parsed manifest JSON (with server-computed coverage)
GET  /api/attempts/:id/export-arm       — auto-generate ARM bundle
GET  /api/schemas/arm-manifest/v1       — ARM manifest JSON Schema
Getting Started
Submit an attempt and use the export endpoint to auto-generate a starter manifest, or run the skeleton generator below. Both hand you arm_version: "1.0", and nothing on the platform ever writes "1.1" for you. One caveat on the export endpoint: it only generates that starter manifest when the attempt has no bundle yet. Once you have uploaded a bundle, export returns that upload back to you byte for byte, so what you get is whatever arm_version you put in it — measured: a fresh attempt exports "1.0", and the same attempt after uploading a v1.1 bundle exports "1.1". Export is a starter only for a bundle-less attempt; after that it is a download. Getting to v1.1 is therefore two edits you make yourself, and the second is the one people miss: add the manifest’s execution block (log_path, exit_code, artifacts), and set arm_version to "1.1". The server does not infer the version from the block being present — arm_version is a declared field, required by the schema and checked only against the enum ["1.0", "1.1"] (measured: "9.9" and a missing field each produce a schema-violation error; "1.0" and "1.1" both pass). Note what is not a manifest edit: characterization.json and trace/trace.jsonl are zip members, and execution is a key in arm_manifest.json, not a directory to create — adding an execution/ directory changes nothing the scanner reads. Or use the skeleton generator:
python scripts/generate_skeleton_bundles.py
Full Protocol Reference
ARM_PROTOCOL_REFERENCE.md (served by the platform; also in the repo at docs/) collects the schema and design background — but read it as history, not as the contract. It self-reports Status: Community Draft v1.0 and is behind the server in at least three places: it says the optional modalities lift the scorecard, it puts the trace timestamp window at ran_at ± wall_time_s (the validator actually allows [ran_at − slack, ran_at + slack + wall_time_s] with slack = max(2 × wall_time_s, 10 min) — an asymmetric window, the upper edge carrying an extra wall_time_s; measured with ran_at=00:00:00Z, wall_time_s=600, a step at +30:00 is accepted and +31:00 warns, while −20:00 is accepted and −21:00 warns), and it lists the old draft → packaging → incomplete | ready → verified | failed state machine. Where it and this page disagree, this page is the one checked against the code. GET /api/protocol used to be behind this page in four places; three of them have since been corrected at the source and this paragraph was rewritten with them: execution artifacts are scanned under results/* at the bundle root, the anti-fraud checks do not feed trace_quality at all, and the timestamp window is [ran_at - slack, ran_at + slack + wall_time_s] with slack = max(2 * wall_time_s, 10 minutes). The fourth is still true but is now published honestly rather than silently: environment_reproducibility ships with dimension_is_computed: false because nothing writes it. On trace_quality read the descriptor rather than this sentence: the tiers only run once the trace has been extracted - bundle validation can return before that, and then the value stays at what the first stage set from mere file presence.
